newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PLAYER GETS $410,000 AFTER BAD TACKLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLAYER GETS $410,000 AFTER BAD TACKLE.

text.p: In the first case of its kind in Britain, a former soccer player was awarded 250,000 pounds ($410,000) in damages on Thursday after a tackle by another player ended his career.
Brian McCord of Stockport County, currently of the English second division, had sued for compensation after Swansea City captain John Cornforth badly damaged his right leg in a game in 1993.
The judgement could have serious implications for the game, since all previous such attempts by soccer players to sue for damages had been thrown out.
McCord's solicitor John England said the decision was a landmark because there was no system for players to obtain compensation for injuries received during games.
"I believe it is time for the sporting bodies to devise some system of compensation without redress to the courts," he said.
The judge said Cornforth had not taken reasonable care when making the tackle, which expert witnesses told the court was one of the worst they had ever seen.

"I didn't take my eye off the ball and I saw Cornforth approach and as I made contact with the ball his leg was resting above the ball and the next thing I knew I saw my grossly deformed right leg," said McCord, now 28.
"I can look forward to Christmas now, but I would much rather that my career had been left intact," said the player, who is training to be a physiotherapist.
